resources.string: A small server in your exe.dev account, with an HTTPS address
For every assistant here. Tried once before it is kept.
With it and a backup, everything on this server can be brought back. Keep it away from the server, and the passphrase in your password manager.
The backup key, sealed with a passphrase
Everything on it goes for good, and nothing is kept: make a recovery kit and download a backup first if you need one. Type %1$s to remove it.
Not running: check the server\'s log
Set here, for every assistant. Tap to change it.
None yet. Tap to add your key.
Your devices stop managing it. You stay its owner, and nothing on the server changes.
Deletes %1$s from your exe.dev account, with its assistants, their history and the backups on it.
Send them this link, or have them type the code %1$s in the Nudge app. It works once, for ten minutes.
You joined it from home: its rooms are beside your own.
%1$s (add a key on the server first)
Me: I join it from my home, and keep one sign-in
Someone else: it is their home, and they are its admin
Your home has no address yet.
Its rooms, history and memory go. The server keeps a backup for 30 days. Type %1$s to delete it.
Said to the model before every conversation
Its rooms show beside your home\'s, and you are its admin and an owner of this server.
This server\'s Nudge is older than Wired. It installs new releases itself; check for one now.
Your servers stop reaching each other through this network.
This server leaves the network, and stops reaching your other servers through it.
Use http://nudge.%1$s.wired as your home\'s address?
Your other servers then reach your home over Wired. Your home\'s address is who it is to other assistants: the ones you joined from home have to be joined again.
It no longer reaches your servers over Wired, and can\'t join again with its key. A new server can then use the name.
Installing %1$s. The server restarts in a minute; come back then.
Lowercase letters, digits and dashes, such as box.
Or join one: hold a network on your home server first, then come back here.
This server\'s release has no Wired.
Remove a server from the network when it\'s gone: a new server can then take its name.
No server with a public address has joined yet: open one of them here and join this network.
Your servers reach each other over Wired, encrypted, with no port open at home: home holds the network, and servers with a public address join it.
The server didn\'t join home\'s Wired network.
The server is still joining home\'s Wired network. Try again in a minute.
